messages:
sofia: Heads up — saw a sharp p99/p999 spike on the KV-heavy long-context stress run earlier. Looks like eviction happened mid-generation and latency exploded.

raj: Do you have the run id + a few log lines? Any sign of correctness errors (wrong tokens) or just latency?

sofia: Run id `stress-2026-03-17-18`. Early logs:
```
evict-bot: eviction_triggered pool=gdpu-2 policy=lru freed=3 entries total_freed_bytes=2457600
2026-03-17T18:12:33Z [runtime] kv: lookup miss -> paging(0x7f9d)
2026-03-17T18:12:33Z [runtime] kv: allocate slot id=1024 owner=req-5412
2026-03-17T18:12:33Z [runtime] kv: read slot id=1024 len=8192 -> returned data for different ctx id=998
```
That second-to-last line is the scary one — token stream contained words from previous context. Not just tail latency.

mei: Ugh. That looks like slot reuse without synchronization. Could be non-atomic zeroing or missing generation tag check. I just repro'd locally with a microstress (200 concurrent streams, sequence len 12k).

me: repro steps i used: `KV_CONCURRENCY=200 KV_DEBUG=1 ./tools/kv_stress --longctx --iter 5000`

raj: If it's a reuse bug we should add a per-slot generation counter (increment on eviction) and require generation match on lookup. Treat mismatch as miss + recount. That often buys safety without too much perf cost.

jordan: FYI I ran FIFO vs LRU microbench last week. Under steady state FIFO had slightly lower p99 on high-throughput (fewer metadata ops), but under heavy burst FIFO caused higher memory churn which can spike GC/alloc latency.

sofia: The interesting part here is under pressure we saw lots of evict_ops/sec (~1.2k/s) and interleaved reads/writes. I think the runtime was freeing a slot, another thread grabbed the pointer, then a paged write completed and wrote data for the old owner -> corruption.

evict-bot: automatic: pool=gdpu-2 pressure=high evict_policy=lru evict_ops=1248 last_evicted_id=1024

mei: I pushed a branch (me/kv/gen-check) that adds a 32-bit generation counter to header and checks it on read. Results: correctness failures drop to 0 but p99 only down from 650ms -> 320ms under the same stress (concurrency 200). Still high.

sofia: Can you paste perf counters from that run? I want evict/sec, avg_evicted_size, page_faults/sec, stall_time_ms.

mei: Perf dump: `evict_ops/sec=1248, avg_evicted_size=7.8KB, page_faults/sec=920, kv_stall_ms_p99=310, kv_stall_ms_p999=980`

raj: So gen-counter fixes correctness but not tail. Two hypotheses: 1) eviction path serializes with lookups and creates contention, 2) our kernel selection path (memory copy vs fast-path) chooses slow path when slot near reused. We need profiling.

jordan: I added a lightweight atomic CAS on slot->state so eviction becomes atomic (marking as EVICTING). That reduces races and also lets lookups skip without waiting. In my local run patch (jordan/kv/atomic-evict) p99 dropped to ~280ms. FIFO variant with same atomic change got p99 ~220ms but memory footprint grew ~8% under sustained burst.

perf-ci: queued job 5402: `kv-stress --concurrency 200 --iters 5000 --branches jordan/kv/atomic-evict`

perf-ci: results job 5402: baseline p99=650ms, mei/gen-check p99=320ms, jordan/atomic-evict p99=280ms, jordan/atomic-evict+fifo p99=220ms. Correctness failures: baseline=4, mei/gen-check=0, jordan/atomic-evict=0, atomic+fifo=0. Memory delta: atomic=+2%, atomic+fifo=+8%.

sofia: Great. So plan: ship gen-counter as safety net and atomic eviction for correctness+latency. FIFO maybe as opt-in heuristic for certain workloads where p99 is critical and memory headroom exists.

raj: Agreed. Action items: 1) mei -> merge gen-check (safety net + logs) 2) jordan -> refine atomic-evict (reduce CAS hotspots, add backoff) 3) sofia -> add runtime flag `kv.eviction_policy=fifo|lru|adaptive` and set adaptive default to lru for dedicated, fifo opt-in for host-api bursts. 4) eng-sre -> monitor mem growth alert on FIFO.

sofia: I'll open a short RFC + rollout plan with perf numbers and a canary policy. Can we also add an emergency fallback so if memory delta > 5% we auto-switch eviction_policy back to lru?

jordan: Will prototype auto-fallback.

raj: One more small fix: add event `kv.eviction.generation_mismatch` to telemetry so we can detect attempted reuse in prod without enabling debug logs.

sofia: Nice. If nobody objects I'll start the RFC and schedule a canary tomorrow 0800 UTC. :thumbsup:

mei: no objections. I'll queue the merge and a perf retest after Jordan's CAS optimizations. :+1:

jordan: ping me if perf after CAS still shows hotspots, I'll add per-shard backoffs.

evict-bot: automation: rolling canary scheduled for pool=gdpu-2 at 2026-03-18T08:00:00Z

perf-ci: job 5402: archived results -> link: https://perf-ci/reports/5402 (internal)

sofia: Thanks all. Short follow-up: keep the reproduction harness and the `--longctx` flags so we can run nightly sanity.

raj: noted.

(meeting end)
